messages:
Nina L.: Quick review request: new Revoke Key designs up in Figma. Deciding between inline revoke + undo toast vs modal confirm for high-risk keys. Need copy + a11y feedback. Link: https://figma.com/file/zxy999/revoke-ux

Omar V.: Inline toast is less disruptive for scoped keys. For production keys I'd prefer typed confirm (TYPE REVOKE) to force intent.

Clara (a11y): Accessibility checklist: toast must be asserted to SRs and include an accessible 'Undo' button. Typed confirm modal needs focus trap, aria-describedby for the danger text, and label the text input clearly.

Ben T.: Backend note: undo window = 15s requires soft-revoke state. Typed confirm = extra step but okay. We should also create an audit log entry immediately and mark undone events.

Nina L.: Copy suggestions: Toast: "Key revoked — Undo" (actionable). Modal heading: "Revoke API key"; blurb: "Revoking removes access immediately. This may break services. Type REVOKE to proceed." CTA: "Revoke key" (danger).

Omar V.: For empty state after final revoke, show a compact card with primary button "Create key" and a secondary link "Key best practices". Make primary first in tab order. Also include 3 bullet tips (scoped, ephemeral, rotate).

Clara (a11y): Ensure bullets are semantic list elements and CTAs have visible focus styles. Alt text for any illustration. If we expose admin-only modal, document that screen readers will announce role="dialog" and the reason field must be aria-required when visible.

Nina L.: Action items: Omar to update figma with typed-confirm modal variation; Ben to confirm soft-revoke feasibility; Clara to run quick SR pass on both flows. Will reconvene tomorrow.
